consolidatedFindings.title: Permissionless collectReward advances accPromoPerShare during the promo Flushing window, leaving phantom promo pending after finalize (cross-staker theft or claim DoS)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: collectReward L559-573 (permissionless _updatePool trigger), promo accrual _updatePool L753-762, batchClaim debt-align L456, finalizePromotion L482-496
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: The rotation flush's load-bearing guarantee is that batchClaim aligns EVERY staker's promoDebt to the CURRENT accPromoPerShare so that once the promo is finalized every staker's promo pending is exactly zero and the next promotion (which reuses the never-reset accumulator) starts from zero. accPromoPerShare can still be advanced AFTER the flush has aligned debts but BEFORE finalizePromotion clears promoToken: any _updatePool during the Flushing phase (promoToken still set, time elapsed) bumps the accumulator past the aligned debts. The primary trigger is the PERMISSIONLESS collectReward (no onlyOwner, no whenNotPaused) which runs _updatePool first; secondary owner-footgun triggers are setDepletionDuration and setDesiredAPY (both call _updatePool during Flushing, neither whenNotPaused-gated). setPromoDepletionDuration is NOT a trigger (phase-gated to Active).
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Pool-size dependent: (a) THEFT — if the next promotion's pool covers the phantom over-credit, the over-credited staker claims promo tokens never earned in that promotion, draining co-stakers (PoC: alice retains 42,857e18 phantom pending post-finalize, claims 42,857 partner2 tokens at t=0 with zero stake time in the new promo); (b) DoS — if the phantom exceeds the next pool, the credited staker's legitimate claim reverts ERC20InsufficientBalance (PoC: 1,142,857e18 credit vs 1,000,000e18 pool). Token custody conservation (funded==paidOut+held) still holds; corruption lives in the per-share accumulator/debt space and surfaces as mis-crediting BETWEEN stakers.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: PM-003 (Linear-Depletion recurrence check) and the econ-scan linearDepletionVerdict both concluded the promo stream's rate-drift is MITIGATED — that conclusion is CORRECT for the rate-recompute path (no permissionless promo re-rate) but INCOMPLETE: the invariant fuzzer found a DISTINCT accumulator-advance-during-flush defect that the static mitigation reasoning did not cover. This finding supersedes the 'promo mitigated / not-reborn' note for the Flushing window specifically. SA-023's 'review the NEW promo accrual window at boundaries' concern is the realized bug here.
consolidatedFindings.distinctFrom: DEDUP-05 (collectReward stable-window reset): both live in collectReward and both exploit its permissionless _updatePool, but DEDUP-01's root cause is accPromoPerShare advancing past aligned promoDebts during Flushing (cross-staker mis-credit, High), whereas DEDUP-05 is the stable rewardPerSecond re-anchor (emission-timing grief, Low). Keep separate.

poc.result: 2 passed (theft + DoS cases); invariants broke at 14 runs/840 calls (P3) and 30 runs/1800 calls (P4), reverts:0

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Gate promo accrual in _updatePool on promoPhase != Flushing (freezes the promo stream during the flush; closes all three trigger paths at the accrual site). Alternatives (whenNotPaused on collectReward; snapshot/pin accPromoPerShare at beginFlush) are partial or more complex.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: NEW High for this run — not a carried-forward ledger item. Regression-check that the promo family Linear-Depletion memo ('do NOT auto-suppress') is honored: this is a fresh, distinct sub-bug of that family.

consolidatedFindings.title: MigratorV2V3.migrate bricks the whole chunk on a single reverting/blocklisted reward recipient, with no in-contract recovery (reseed forbidden mid-pass)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/MigratorV2V3.sol: reward forwards L187/L190/L193 (safeTransfer, reverting), reseed guard L114 (require(!seeded || migrateIterator==-1)), withdrawAll L216-229 (no pass reset), userInfo tuple read L160
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: migrate() forwards each user's three reward deltas (phUSD L187, stable L190, promo L193) with reverting safeTransfer inside a sequential loop that cannot skip an index. A single recipient that cannot receive any one token (realistically an OFAC/compliance-frozen or blocklisted USDC/USDT address that was a legitimate V2 staker at seed time, or a restricted partner promoToken) reverts the entire migrate() and every index >= that cursor. There is NO in-contract recovery: seedUsers requires !seeded || migrateIterator==-1 so a fresh straggler list excluding the bad address is forbidden while the cursor is pinned (>=0, !=-1); withdrawAll is a pure balance sweep that does not reset the pass; migrate cannot advance. Only recovery is deploying a new MigratorV2V3 and re-wiring via setMigrator on BOTH V2 and V3.
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Liveness/availability DoS of the entire remaining V2->V3 migration. No theft, no principal loss (V2/V3 positions intact; withdrawAll recovers stranded balances). Owner-recoverable only via redeploy+rewire, so ceiling is Medium. Asymmetry: V3.batchClaim solved exactly this failure mode with the non-reverting _tryTransfer + unclaimablePromo banking; MigratorV2V3.migrate did not adopt the same pattern.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: SA-005's reentrancy sub-claim on migrate is REFUTED (ECON-N1: netting correct, counterparties trusted, no theft); the retained substance from SA-005/SA-018/SA-019 is the unbounded cross-contract batch loop + discarded userInfo tuple that compound the same availability brick. F-01 adds the story-self-contradiction layer: the contract NatSpec offers 'exclude such addresses from the seed list' as the operational escape, but the same doc's 'reseeding mid-pass is forbidden' + the L114 guard make that escape UNREACHABLE while bricked — the true recovery is only a full redeploy (Law-2 false-recovery-promise, lawImpacted:2).

poc.sketch: Seed [A, BLOCKED, C] where BLOCKED is a USDC-blocklisted address with a V2 stable-reward accrual. migrate(3): A migrates, BLOCKED's rewardToken.safeTransfer reverts -> whole tx reverts, migrateIterator stays 0. seedUsers([A,C]) reverts 'pass in progress'. migrate(3) reverts forever. Assert cursor cannot reach -1 without a new migrator. (pocSketch present in CODE-001.)

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Wrap the three reward forwards in a non-reverting try-transfer (reuse _tryTransfer/unclaimablePromo bank), OR let migrate skip a failing index, OR relax the reseed guard to allow an owner mid-pass re-seed excluding a poisoned address. Correct the NatSpec recovery note to state redeploy is the only escape once bricked.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: Same envelope as ledger V2-M-01 (MigratorV1V2 strict-== brick: availability only, owner recovery, no theft) but re-expressed on the NEW V3 migrator as a transfer-revert rather than a balance precondition. Sanitizer to reconcile by fingerprint; likely a fresh Medium instance rather than a pure ledger dup.

consolidatedFindings.title: emergencyTransfer during an active promo leaves stale promo bookkeeping, bricking stake/withdraw/claim for stakers with pending promo on resume
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: emergencyTransfer L307-325 (sweeps promo, does NOT reset promoToken/promoRewardBalance/promoPhase), promo accrual _updatePool L753-762, promo payout _claimRewards L800-807 (reverts on zero balance)
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: emergencyTransfer sweeps all phUSD/reward/promo balances to a recipient and pauses, but does NOT touch promo bookkeeping (promoToken stays set, promoRewardBalance stays >0, promoPhase stays Active) nor staking accounting. After the sweep the contract believes it owes promo it no longer holds. On unpause (permitted because phase==Active, not Flushing), the first user interaction runs _updatePool which keeps accruing accPromoPerShare against the phantom promoRewardBalance, so users show positive pendingPromo, and _claimRewards' promo leg does a reverting promoToken.safeTransfer against a zero balance — reverting the user's stake/withdraw/claim. Every existing staker with pending promo is bricked out of all three core functions.
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Post-emergency availability DoS of core user functions for any staker with pending promo; principal (phUSD) unwithdrawable through the normal path until recovery, and already-accrued promo is forfeited (swept to recipient). No direct theft. Recovery is available but NON-obvious: unpause -> beginFlush (re-pauses) -> drive batchClaim to completion (its _tryTransfer banks the now-unpayable promo into unclaimablePromo, so the flush itself does not brick) -> finalizePromotion (clears promoToken/promoRewardBalance, aligns debts to pending==0) -> unpause. Owner-recoverable, no fund loss beyond the intended emergency drain, hence Medium/Low. Owner FOOTGUN (Law 3): a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised that the break-glass + unpause bricks staking.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: TWO compounding root causes are folded here per task instruction, but they are DISTINCT and should be surfaced as such downstream: (a) PRIMARY / NEW V3 — the promo-specific stale-accounting brick on resume (ECON-001 + CODE-005), which is the substantive Medium; (b) SECONDARY / CARRIED-FORWARD — PM-005's pauseWithdraw-reverts-on-drained-phUSD spec-conformance item, which is the ledger F-01/V2-F-01 issue re-appearing verbatim in V3 (owner drain is a KNOWING action; route to spec-conformance channel, not a fresh H/M). They live in the same function and compound (post-drain, pauseWithdraw is also unavailable), which is why they are consolidated, but the sanitizer should reconcile PM-005's sub-part against ledger F-01/V2-F-01 while treating the promo-stale part (a) as a new V3 finding.

poc.sketch: Owner has Active promo (promoToken set, promoRewardBalance>0). emergencyTransfer(treasury) sweeps all incl. promo + pauses. Owner refunds phUSD+stable, unpause(). Any staker with pending promo: stake/withdraw/claim reverts inside _claimRewards promo transfer (zero balance). Assert recovery requires the full beginFlush->batchClaim->finalizePromotion dance before unpause.

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: In emergencyTransfer, when a promo slot is set, also reset promo bookkeeping (promoToken=0, promoRewardBalance=0, promoPhase=None, promoRewardPerSecond=0), OR gate _updatePool/_claimRewards promo accrual on actual on-hand balance. At minimum, document the mandatory post-emergency finalize-flush before any unpause.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: Primary (promo-stale) = new V3 Medium footgun. Secondary (PM-005 pauseWithdraw) reconciles to ledger F-01 (V1) / V2-F-01 (V2) spec-conformance — sanitizer to confirm it is tracked for V3 rather than re-filed fresh.

consolidatedFindings.title: Uncapped, unbacked phUSD reward mint on the phUSD leg (config-conditional: immunized only by zero-APY default)
consolidatedFindings.severityEstimate: High-conditional (Medium/QA at zero-APY; High if any non-zero APY config ships)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: phUSD accrual L744-746 (NO cap), mint L781-784, emission rate L831 (phUSDPerSecond = totalStaked*desiredAPYBps/10000/SECONDS_PER_YEAR), setDesiredAPY two-step L222-240
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: The phUSD reward leg is minted on demand with NO funded-budget cap, unlike the stable leg (capped at rewardBalance L730) and promo leg (capped at promoRewardBalance L756). _updatePool accrues phUSDReward = timeElapsed * phUSDPerSecond with no cap; _claimRewards mints it unbacked via phUSD.mint. phUSDPerSecond is zero whenever desiredAPYBps==0 (the shipped/constructor default, KI-10 immunization). The moment the owner commits any non-zero APY via the two-step setDesiredAPY, phUSD is minted on demand, unbacked, with no per-window cap and no upper bound on desiredAPYBps. Total annual issuance == totalStaked*desiredAPYBps/10000 — intended inflation-by-emission, single _updatePool writer, no double-mint/over-mint accounting bug found (pendingPhUSD view mirrors).
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Config-conditional dilution of all phUSD holders / backing-ratio erosion of a token meant to be a stablecoin. Worked example: totalStaked=10M, desiredAPYBps=500 (5%) => 500,000 phUSD/yr minted with zero collateral. Non-obvious owner footgun on the APY magnitude (no upper bound => fat-finger silently mints large unbacked phUSD). Currently immunized ONLY by the zero-APY default.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: story-faithfulness explicitly rules this NOT-A-FINDING as deliberate documented design (SolvencyDetermination.md 2: phUSD minted on demand, no pre-funded pool, solvency = active mint privilege). The symbolic result (zero-APY immunization PROVEN) corroborates the gating. Therefore this is a config-conditional / known-concern regression carried verbatim from V2, NOT a fresh independent High. Kept as a single consolidated finding and explicitly FLAGGED for the sanitizer to reconcile against the ledger/known-issues rather than dropped here (per Law 1 + task instruction).

poc.reason: Intended-emission-by-design; no exploit accounting bug. Would only be a finding if a non-zero-APY config is in scope for this run, in which case it becomes a config/severity call, not a coded exploit.

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Confirm the deployed config ships desiredAPYBps==0 (KI-10). If any non-zero APY is intended, gate the phUSD leg against a funded/authorized emission budget or bound desiredAPYBps, and document the unbacked-mint invariant.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: Reconciles to ledger V2-M-02 (phUSD mint authority load-bearing) and V2-M-03 (memory: 're-classify HIGH if any non-zero-APY config ships'; zero-APY/KI-10 currently immunizes). Sanitizer decides: suppress under KI-10/known-issue if zero-APY config is confirmed in scope; else emit at honest (High) severity. DO NOT DROP at dedup.

consolidatedFindings.title: Permissionless collectReward re-anchors the STABLE rewardPerSecond depletion window (emission-timing griefing)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: collectReward L559-573, rate recompute L570 (rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance*PRECISION/depletionDuration)
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: collectReward is permissionless (require only amount>0) and is the recompute site for the stable stream: it runs _updatePool at the old rate, pulls `amount` rewardToken, then re-anchors rewardPerSecond over a FRESH full depletionDuration from now. Anyone can call collectReward(1 wei) repeatedly to perpetually reset the depletion window, stretching stable emission toward zero rate.
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Griefing of stable reward emission TIMING only — no theft, funds stay in rewardBalance and eventually distribute, no redistribution between stakers (uniform slow-down). Turns linear depletion into ~exponential decay (~63% distributed by nominal window end instead of 100%). Attacker pays gas + 1 wei per call indefinitely with no profit; self-limiting. Could be argued Medium as an availability impact.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: Inherited-from-V2 pattern now present in NEW V3 code. Kept SEPARATE from DEDUP-01 despite sharing the collectReward permissionless _updatePool entrypoint: different root cause (stable rate re-anchor vs promo accumulator advance past aligned debts) and different impact (timing grief vs cross-staker theft/DoS). The econ-scan linearDepletionVerdict flags this as the surviving permissionless residual of the Linear-Depletion family (stable leg only; promo re-rate sites are onlyOwner).

poc.reason: Mechanism is deterministic and clear; a coded PoC would show emission-schedule stretch but adds little to a Low grief. Severity-classifier to weigh Low vs Medium.

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Restrict collectReward to the funder/owner role, or anchor the recompute to the REMAINING window rather than a fresh full depletionDuration so a third party cannot re-anchor.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: Inherited from V2 (present there too). Sanitizer to check whether the V2 instance is already a ledger item; the V3 recurrence should be tracked.

consolidatedFindings.title: _tryTransfer abi.decode reverts on short (1-31 byte) returndata, bricking a batchClaim chunk despite the 'flush must never brick' guarantee
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: _tryTransfer computes callSuccess && (returndata.length==0 || abi.decode(returndata,(bool))) with no length check. A promoToken whose transfer succeeds at the call level but returns NON-empty returndata shorter than 32 bytes fails the length==0 short-circuit, so abi.decode into a bool is evaluated — which requires exactly a 32-byte word and REVERTS on shorter data. The revert propagates out of _tryTransfer (not wrapped in try) and reverts the whole batchClaim chunk, defeating the explicit 'the flush must never brick' design intent. flushCursor can never reach _stakers.length(), so finalizePromotion is unreachable and the promo slot becomes permanently un-rotatable.
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Flush/rotation DoS for a class of non-standard promo token. Token-assumption dependent (promoToken is owner-vetted per promotion), so Low; no fund loss.
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: SA-016 (raw low-level call in _tryTransfer, flagged for return-value interpretation review) is the static-analyzer's surfacing of the same primitive; CODE-003 confirms the exact decode-revert edge; F-02 records it as a Law-2 contradiction of the documented 'never brick' invariant (banking design itself is faithful; the decode edge undermines it). Primary ownership + severity sit with the code scanner.

poc.reason: Requires a mock promo token returning 1-31 byte returndata; straightforward but Low and gated behind owner token-vetting.

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Length-check returndata (>=32) before abi.decode and treat any non-standard/short returndata as a failed transfer (bank into unclaimablePromo) rather than letting it revert.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: New V3 Low. No prior ledger item expected.

consolidatedFindings.title: MigratorV2V3.withdrawAll escape hatch does not sweep the promo token (incomplete token coverage)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/MigratorV2V3.sol: withdrawAll L216-229 (sweeps only phUSD + rewardToken, not promoToken)

consolidatedFindings.title: Zombie staker set entries: pauseWithdraw-to-zero leaves users in _stakers, monotonically inflating owner flush cost
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: pauseWithdraw L533-552 (deliberately does NOT touch _stakers), invariant 'membership <=> amount>0' L611-612, batchClaim visit L452
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: A user who fully exits via pauseWithdraw (amount->0) is NOT removed from _stakers (by design, to keep the set frozen during a flush), breaking the stated invariant 'membership <=> userInfo.amount > 0'. Zombie entries are correctness-harmless (batchClaim visits them with pending==0 and aligns promoDebt to 0) but accumulate across pause cycles, monotonically inflating the per-rotation flush iteration count / gas the owner pays to reach flushCursor == _stakers.length().
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: No fund risk; flush is chunked so no hard brick. Zombies only form during an owner/pauser pause window (user must have staked >= MINIMUM_STAKE first), so not cheaply spammable by a third party without a pause window. Low/QA operational footgun.
sourceIds: SA-017(cross-ref: unused _stakers.add/remove return -> confirm no enumeration desync)
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: code-scan CONFIRMED harmless-but-noted; pattern-matcher matched. SA-017 (ignored EnumerableSet add/remove return) is cross-referenced here because it concerns the same _stakers enumeration integrity batchClaim depends on; the retained question ('can double-add/missing-remove desync enumeration') is answered by this finding (only zero-amount zombies accumulate; no desync, EnumerableSet dedupes adds).
consolidatedFindings.recommendation: Document that stakerCount can exceed active stakers; optionally allow a permissionless compaction pass that removes zero-amount members outside a flush.

consolidatedFindings.title: startPromotion / topUpPromotion strict balance-delta equality reverts on fee-on-transfer / donated / rebasing promo token (funding brick)
consolidatedFindings.location: src/PhlimboV3.sol: startPromotion strict-eq L349-351, topUpPromotion strict-eq L377-379, plus state-after-external-call on the same funding admin paths
consolidatedFindings.rootCause: startPromotion and topUpPromotion require an EXACT balance delta (IERC20(token).balanceOf(this)-balanceBefore == amount). A fee-on-transfer/rebasing promo token, or an unsolicited donation front-run that perturbs balanceOf, makes the delta != amount and reverts the funding call. Also flagged: state written after the transferFrom on these owner-invoked funding paths (SA-027).
consolidatedFindings.impactSummary: Griefable/DoS of promo FUNDING (owner-invoked, retryable). No theft, no principal risk. The balance-delta assertion is arguably an INTENTIONAL fee-on-transfer rejection (owner vets the promo token per promotion).
consolidatedFindings.reconciliation: Not one of the task's 8 named clusters, but retained (Law 1 recall) rather than dropped. Pattern-matcher checkedNoMatch FEE-ON-TRANSFER-ACCOUNTING explicitly treats this balance-delta assertion as an intended fee-on-transfer rejection (promo token owner-vetted, weird-token OOS). SA-027's reentrancy-on-owner-funding is an owner KNOWING action (Law 3) with an owner-vetted token, so it is folded here as a related note, not a separate reentrancy finding.

poc.reason: Funding-time revert on a non-standard/donated token; owner-retryable, no exploit path.

consolidatedFindings.recommendation: If fee-on-transfer promo tokens are ever intended in scope, credit the observed delta instead of asserting exact equality; otherwise document the exact-transfer requirement for promo tokens.
consolidatedFindings.ledgerReconcileHint: Reconciles to C4 known-invalid classes (fee-on-transfer / non-standard ERC20 unless in scope). Sanitizer/validity-checker to decide suppression; kept here so the decision is explicit, not silent.
